title: How to Restore the Classic Power Off Menu and Disable Gemini Power Button Hijack
metaTitle: Restore Classic Power Off Menu & Disable Gemini Hijack (2026)
metaDescription: Holding your phone's power button launches Google Gemini or Assistant instead of the Power Off / Restart menu? Step-by-step guide to restoring the classic power menu on Android.
metaKeywords: disable gemini power button, restore classic power menu android, hold power button power off samsung, turn off google assistant power button android
excerpt: Modern Android updates hijacked the physical power button to launch Gemini AI instead of letting you turn off your phone. Here is how to restore the traditional power menu.
description: Comprehensive tutorial on reclaiming the physical hardware power button across Samsung One UI, Google Pixel, Xiaomi HyperOS, and OnePlus to restore the traditional Power Off, Restart, and Emergency menu.
altImage: Diagram showing how to change the hardware side key gesture from digital assistant to the classic Power Off menu

faq.title: Why did smartphone manufacturers replace the Power Off menu with digital assistants?
faq.description: Tech giants (Google, Samsung, and Apple) repurposed the physical power button (now rebranded as the 'Side Button') into a dedicated hardware trigger for conversational AI assistants (Gemini, Bixby, and Siri) to drive daily active user engagement, forcing users to use awkward two-button combinations (Power + Volume Up) to shut down.

faq.title: Can I still access Google Gemini or Assistant if I reassign the power button?
faq.description: Yes! Reclaiming the physical power button does NOT disable Gemini. You can still invoke Gemini instantly by swiping up diagonally from either bottom corner of your display, using the hands-free voice prompt 'Hey Google', or tapping the microphone icon in the Google search widget.

faq.title: How do I turn off my phone if the power button is broken or frozen?
faq.description: Swipe down twice from the top of your display to expand the Quick Settings notification shade. In the upper-right corner next to the Settings gear icon, tap the software Power icon. This brings up the complete Power Off, Restart, and Emergency SOS menu on screen.

html:
The Frustration of the Hijacked Hardware Button

Few user experience changes in modern operating systems have caused as much widespread consumer irritation as the repurposing of the smartphone power button. For over a decade, holding down the physical button on the right edge of any mobile phone produced a simple, predictable, and critical outcome: a full-screen menu displaying Power Off, Restart, and Emergency Mode.

With recent updates to Android 12 through Android 15—and across custom OEM skins like Samsung One UI, Xiaomi HyperOS, OnePlus OxygenOS, and Google Pixel OS—holding down that very same button now triggers a glowing digital assistant overlay: Google Gemini or Google Assistant. If your phone freezes, begins overheating, or you simply wish to turn off your device before boarding an airplane or entering a cinema, you are greeted by an AI chatbot asking: 'How can I help you today?' Meanwhile, turning off your phone now requires an awkward two-handed claw grip pressing both the Power + Volume Up buttons simultaneously.

Fortunately, you do not have to endure this design choice. The underlying Android operating system still contains native configuration toggles that allow you to restore the classic, instantaneous Power Off menu. This comprehensive tutorial walks you through reversing the Gemini hijack across every major smartphone manufacturer.

Why Device Manufacturers Changed the Default Behavior

The push to rebrand the physical power key into a 'Side Key' or 'Assistant Key' is driven by the strategic race for artificial intelligence adoption. By binding conversational AI agents directly to the most frequently pressed hardware button on the phone, tech giants ensure high daily active user engagement. However, in critical real-world situations—such as a runaway app draining battery, an unresponsive touch digitizer, or an emergency reboot requirement—software-based assistant triggers hinder device control.

Reclaiming the Power Button Across Smartphone Brands

1. Samsung Galaxy (One UI 5, 6, and 7)

Samsung calls the physical power button the 'Side Button'. Here is how to restore the traditional menu:

  1. Open the Settings app on your Samsung Galaxy device.
  2. Scroll down and tap Advanced features.
  3. Tap on Side button.
  4. Under the section labeled 'Press and hold', you will observe two options:
    • Wake Bixby (Default)
    • Power off menu
  5. Select Power off menu.
  6. Bonus Customization: Under the 'Double press' section, you can configure double-tapping the button to immediately launch the Camera app or any custom application of your choice.

2. Google Pixel (Android 12, 13, 14, and 15)

Google Pixel devices introduced the 'Hold for Assistant' gesture in Android 12. To revert it back to the power menu:

  1. Open Settings on your Pixel phone.
  2. Scroll down and select System.
  3. Tap on Gestures.
  4. Scroll to the bottom and select Press & hold power button.
  5. You will see a toggle switch labeled 'Hold for Assistant'. Toggle this switch to OFF.
  6. On newer Pixel builds running Android 14/15, select the radio button labeled Power menu instead of Digital assistant.
  7. Now, holding the power button immediately reveals Power off, Restart, and Lockdown options.

3. OnePlus, Realme, and OPPO (OxygenOS / Realme UI / ColorOS)

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Scroll down and tap Additional settings (or System settings).
  3. Tap on Power button.
  4. Select Press and hold the power button.
  5. Switch the selection from Voice Assistant to Power menu.

4. Xiaomi, Redmi, and POCO (HyperOS / MIUI 14)

  1. Open the Settings application.
  2. Scroll down and tap Additional settings.
  3. Tap on Gesture shortcuts.
  4. Select Launch Google Assistant.
  5. Toggle OFF the option titled 'Press and hold the Power button for 0.5s'.
  6. Xiaomi will immediately restore the traditional four-circle Power Off / Reboot / Airplane Mode / Silent modal.

5. Motorola (Hello UI / My UX)

  1. Open Settings > Gestures.
  2. Tap Press and hold power button.
  3. Switch the preference from Assistant to Power menu.

6. Vivo and iQOO (Funtouch OS)

  1. Open Settings > Shortcuts & accessibility.
  2. Tap on Press and hold the power button.
  3. Select Press and hold the power button from the sub-menu.
  4. Change the selected option from Enable the digital assistant to Enable the power and emergency menu.
  5. Tap confirm. Now, pressing and holding the side key immediately launches the clean reboot and power down interface.

How to Access Gemini Without the Power Button

Restoring your physical power menu does not mean losing access to generative AI features. Android provides multiple superior, non-intrusive gesture triggers:

  • Corner Swipe Gesture: Swipe diagonally upward from either the bottom-left or bottom-right corner of your screen. A vibrant multi-color glow appears, launching Gemini instantly from any screen.
  • Voice Trigger: If enabled in Google app settings, uttering 'Hey Google' wakes Gemini completely hands-free, even when your screen is locked.
  • Home Screen Widget / App Icon: You can place the dedicated Gemini shortcut widget directly on your home screen or dock for one-tap voice and image queries.

What If Your Touchscreen Freezes? The Hardware Force Restart

Understanding hardware key shortcuts is critical during system kernel lockups when the screen fails to register touch input:

  • Universal Android Hard Reboot: Press and hold both the Power Button + Volume Down Button simultaneously for 10 to 12 seconds without letting go.
  • This hardware-level interrupt cuts power directly to the SoC clock generator and forces an immediate cold reboot, completely bypassing any software-level assistant interference or frozen display digitizers.

Android Lockdown Mode: The Lost Security Feature in the Power Menu

One of the most dangerous side effects of Google and Samsung hijacking the physical power button to trigger digital assistants is the loss of one-tap access to Lockdown Mode. Introduced in Android 9, Lockdown is one of the most powerful physical security countermeasures built into any smartphone operating system:

What Lockdown Mode Does When Activated:

  • Disables Biometrics Instantly: Both fingerprint scanning and facial recognition are immediately suppressed at the hardware level. Nobody can force your finger onto the sensor or hold your phone to your face while you are asleep or restrained.
  • Suppresses Lock Screen Notification Previews: All notification banners, SMS preview texts, and OTP alerts are hidden from the lock screen. Only your carrier network status remains visible.
  • Suspends Smart Lock & Trusted Devices: Even if your phone is connected to your home Wi-Fi or paired with a trusted smartwatch, Smart Lock is revoked.
  • Demands Alphanumeric Master Password: The only way to unlock the phone after triggering Lockdown is by manually typing your complex alphanumeric master passphrase.

How to Ensure Lockdown Appears in Your Power Menu:

On Samsung devices running One UI, Lockdown Mode is hidden by default. Once you restore the classic power menu, enable this toggle immediately:

  1. Go to Settings > Lock screen > Secure lock settings.
  2. Enter your current PIN or password.
  3. Toggle ON the option titled: Show Lockdown option.
  4. Now, whenever you press and hold your power button, you will see four distinct buttons: Power off, Restart, Emergency SOS, and Lockdown. If you ever feel in danger or are entering a sensitive public space, one tap on Lockdown instantly armors your device against physical intrusion.

Charging Wattage Curvature & Thermal Stepping Mechanics

Many smartphone buyers believe that an '80W' or '120W' phone charges at that maximum wattage continuously from 0% to 100%. In reality, battery charging follows a strict algorithmic curve dictated by electrochemical safety limits:

  • Phase 1: Peak Pulse (0% to 25%): The charging IC allows maximum rated power (e.g., 100W at 9.2A). Temperatures rise at a steep rate of 1.2°C per minute.
  • Phase 2: First Thermal Step-Down (25% to 65%): As battery voltage crosses 4.1V and internal temperature hits 39°C, the power management chip aggressively drops wattage to 45W to 55W to prevent thermal runaway.
  • Phase 3: Constant Voltage Saturation (65% to 100%): Current steadily tapers down from 30W to 12W, and finally drops to a trickle 4W above 90%.

If your room ambient temperature exceeds 32°C (common across Indian summer months), the phone will trigger Phase 2 thermal step-down almost immediately at 15% charge. Placing your smartphone in front of a gentle desk fan or charging in an air-conditioned room keeps the device beneath the 38°C threshold, allowing high-wattage charging to persist without heating the motherboard.

Preventative Architecture & Companion Recommendations

Reclaiming physical hardware controls over your smartphone restores predictable, frustration-free ergonomics.
